mechanism: "privatebroadcast" is a DEFINE-CORE-ONLY-OPTIONS row (src/config-options.lisp:449) and the feature does not exist: a symbol sweep of BITCOIN-LISP, BITCOIN-LISP.NET and BITCOIN-LISP.RPC finds no symbol whose name contains PRIVATE-BROADCAST, there is no private-broadcast connection type, and neither "abortprivatebroadcast" nor "getprivatebroadcastinfo" is registered in BL.RPC::*RPC-METHODS*. Only the log category name survives (src/logging.lisp:350), with nothing logging under it. Core at d3056bc, on GetBoolArg("-privatebroadcast", DEFAULT_PRIVATE_BROADCAST) (default false, src/net.h:89), raises the connection budget by MAX_PRIVATE_BROADCAST_CONNECTIONS (src/init.cpp:1037-1038, src/net.h:77), turns the feature on in PeerManager options (src/net_processing.h:96) and makes sendrawtransaction take node::TxBroadcast::NO_MEMPOOL_PRIVATE_BROADCAST instead of MEMPOOL_AND_BROADCAST_TO_ALL (src/rpc/mempool.cpp:115-126) -- the transaction is not put in the mempool at all and goes out over short-lived Tor/I2P connections. Two details the finding's core_does understates and that matter to the verdict: Core scopes the option to sendrawtransaction-submitted transactions only ("Transactions submitted through the wallet are not affected", src/init.cpp:687-694), and Core REFUSES TO START with it when neither Tor nor I2P is reachable, or when -connect is also set (InitError at src/init.cpp:2257-2271). Ours starts, warns, and relays through the ordinary announce path.
consequence: An operator who enables it believes a transaction submitted through sendrawtransaction never enters this node's mempool and is announced only over short-lived anonymising connections. Instead it enters the mempool and is announced to every peer from this node's own address, which is the deanonymisation the option exists to prevent. Bounded, and more tightly than the finding states: Core's default is off so only a deliberate opt-in is affected; the option is therefore always supplied, so the startup WARN names it (measured); and on the ordinary clearnet configuration Core would not have run at all, so an operator who sees this node start has already diverged from the Core behaviour they were relying on. The substance is a tracked unbuilt feature -- docs/coverage-vs-core-2026-08-24.md:37-40 lists private broadcast as genuinely missing and docs/next-wave-2026-08-22.md:336-337 sizes it as G7-47 -- so the novel part is only that we accept the flag where Core would refuse to start. Not refuted on the recorded-scoping ground because neither document states this consequence.
evidence: Executed in the project container (worktree /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-options-s3, warm image). (a) (bl.cfg::core-only-option-p "privatebroadcast") => T; START-NODE-PLIST on an argument list including -privatebroadcast=1 returned (:LISTEN T :WALLET-NAMES NIL :NETWORK :REGTEST) with "privatebroadcast" in SUPPLIED-CORE-ONLY-OPTIONS. (b) Symbol sweep over the three packages for names containing "PRIVATE-BROADCAST" returned NIL. (c) RPC table: (gethash "abortprivatebroadcast" bl.rpc::*rpc-methods*) => NIL, (gethash "getprivatebroadcastinfo" ...) => NIL, (gethash "sendrawtransaction" ...) => T -- the one handler that exists is the unconditional mempool-and-relay path. (d) grep over src/networking/ for a private-broadcast connection type or option consumer: none. fix_shape: Two steps, and the cheap one closes the misleading half on its own. First, stop accepting the flag as a no-op: make -privatebroadcast an init-time refusal rather than a core-only row, so a node asked to broadcast privately and unable to refuses to start -- that is closer to Core, which InitErrors whenever the option is set and neither Tor nor I2P is reachable (init.cpp:2261-2265), which is every configuration we could be started in today. Second, if the feature is built later, follow Core's shape: a PRIVATE-BROADCAST connection type with its own budget outside -maxconnections (MAX_PRIVATE_BROADCAST_CONNECTIONS = 64), opened only to randomly chosen Tor/I2P peers and torn down after the announce; a broadcast method selector on the sendrawtransaction path so the transaction bypasses the mempool entirely; and Core's three init checks reproduced verbatim -- reachable Tor/I2P required, incompatible with -connect, and a warning when -proxyrandomize is off. Port the two RPCs (getprivatebroadcastinfo, abortprivatebroadcast) with it, since without them the operator cannot tell whether a private broadcast succeeded. Scope it to sendrawtransaction only; wallet-submitted transactions are explicitly out of scope in Core.
